eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 5, Lesson 25
subtitle: Finding them is mechanical; deciding what they are takes judgment.

caption: The mean (130) is more than double the median (58.5) — the median is robust; one wild value barely moves it.

code:
q1, q3 = s.quantile(0.25), s.quantile(0.75)   # 51.0, 63.5
iqr = q3 - q1                                  # 12.5
low, high = q1 - 1.5*iqr, q3 + 1.5*iqr         # 32.25, 82.25

sales[(s < low) | (s > high)]   # only the 940 order
caption: Beyond 1.5 IQRs past either quartile. Doesn't assume a bell curve — a good default rule.

code:
z = (s - s.mean()) / s.std()
sales[z.abs() > 3]
# same row flagged -- but z-score is only 3.17, barely over the cutoff
caption: The extreme value inflates the std it's judged against — z-scores can miss outliers in small samples.

eyebrow: Decide what the value actually is

steps.label: AN ERROR
steps.sub: Correct it, or treat as missing

code:
sales["is_outlier"] = mask
sales["amount_capped"] = sales["amount"].clip(lower=low, upper=high)
# 940 becomes 82.25

# mean of all 12: 129.83 / mean excluding outlier: 56.18
caption: clip() pulls values back to the fences — keep the original column and the flag for transparency.
